verdicts.target: BARRIER 1: MEMORY TRAFFIC / Gap: PCIe/DRAM traffic volume measurement
verdicts.reason: Step time (67.2 s/step) is measured aggregate; GPU↔CPU bandwidth and latency per phase are not. Cannot determine if PCIe link or contention is a bottleneck. Issue #627 measures commit state and front-load ordering, not GPU-CPU transfer velocity.
verdicts.covering_evidence: None. Issue #627 R2-R5 focus on commit governor, front-load, and loss tracing; PCIe profiling not mentioned.

decisive_experiment.intervention: Enable torch.profiler with GPU/CPU ops tracing; run single step through forward/backward/QAT/optimizer. Capture copy_() kernel durations.
decisive_experiment.measurement: Extract per-phase GPU↔CPU throughput (bytes/duration) from torch.profiler output; compute fraction of theoretical PCIe 4.0 16x peak (≈32 GB/s).
decisive_experiment.kill_condition: If measured throughput is >20 GB/s (≥62% of peak) and GPU-CPU transfer time is <10% of total step time, PCIe is not a bottleneck; else claim investigation warranted.

verdicts.target: BARRIER 1: MEMORY TRAFFIC / Gap: Intra-step peak structure (200-step interior unmonitored)
verdicts.reason: Block governors sample at boundaries only; 200-step interior VRAM transients unknown. Per-parameter loop allocates fresh FP32 grad per call (cpu_offload_adamw.py line 228), creating potential hidden peaks. Issue #627 R5 loss trace ≠ governor reads.
verdicts.covering_evidence: Issue #627 R5 (loss trace) is listed but does not address interior VRAM sampling.

decisive_experiment.intervention: Add per-step (N=0..199) governor checkpoint at training-loop iteration end; log max VRAM and loss to JSONL.
decisive_experiment.measurement: Extract step-to-step VRAM delta from JSONL; compute histogram of interior peaks vs boundary peaks; identify peak-to-trough patterns.
decisive_experiment.kill_condition: If interior peaks never exceed boundary peaks by >500 MiB, claim transient structure is negligible and front-load suffices; else claim interior structure requires intra-step optimization.

verdicts.target: BARRIER 1: MEMORY TRAFFIC / Gap: Step time attribution (no per-phase breakdown)
verdicts.reason: Measured 67.2 s/step is monolithic. No breakdown of forward/backward/QAT/optimizer/IO phases. Cannot prioritize optimization without phase-level visibility.
verdicts.covering_evidence: None. No active issue tracks per-phase timing; step-trace-cbase-grow-rung2 receipt exists but lacks per-phase aggregation.

decisive_experiment.intervention: Use torch.profiler kernel-level tracing or nvidia-smi with 10ms polling to segment step into (a) forward, (b) backward, (c) fake-quant, (d) optimizer, (e) save/IO. Instrument per-phase boundary markers in Python.
decisive_experiment.measurement: Log duration per phase (average over 10 consecutive steps); compute fraction of total step time.
decisive_experiment.kill_condition: If no phase exceeds 25% of total, claim phases are balanced; else identify top 2 phases as optimization targets.

verdicts.target: BARRIER 1: MEMORY TRAFFIC / Gap: Activation memory scaling (batch size assumption)
verdicts.reason: Issue #480 is actively running Config C (micro_batch=1) in blocks 5-10. Audit states 'active leg'. Baseline batch=2 logged (10.98 GiB); batch=1 result pending. Two data points sufficient to verify or refute linear assumption.
verdicts.covering_evidence: Issue #480 rung2-stabilize active leg with explicit Config C micro_batch=1 in measured_position.

verdicts.target: BARRIER 1: MEMORY TRAFFIC / Gap: Commit elastic-limit dynamics (expansion latency, page-out contention)
verdicts.reason: Commit governor measures instantaneous state (74.5 GiB observed at block-05); expansion speed, disk I/O contention, and page-fault cascades are unmeasured. Cannot predict if subsequent blocks are safe or will hit wall.
verdicts.covering_evidence: Issue #627 R2 (in-process commit governor, current-state reading) does not address dynamics of elastic expansion or I/O latency.

decisive_experiment.intervention: Run existing test block under Windows Performance Toolkit (ETW) with VirtualMemory + disk I/O providers enabled.
decisive_experiment.measurement: Extract page-file growth trace (size vs time per block); compute expansion latency (time to grow 1 GiB); I/O IOPS histogram and read-latency distribution.
decisive_experiment.kill_condition: If page-file expansion latency is <100ms per GiB and I/O IOPS never exceed 1000, claim elastic expansion is not a bottleneck; else claim it limits throughput.

verdicts.target: BARRIER 1: MEMORY TRAFFIC / Lever: Micro-batch reduction (1 vs 2)
verdicts.reason: Issue #480 Config C explicitly micro_batch=1. Once run completes and VRAM peak is logged, lever is measured. Baseline batch=2 already known (10.98 GiB); batch=1 result will confirm linear scaling and quantify savings.
verdicts.covering_evidence: Issue #480 active leg Config C micro_batch=1.

verdicts.target: BARRIER 1: MEMORY TRAFFIC / Lever: Gradient checkpointing toggle
verdicts.reason: Gradient checkpointing is currently OFF per contract. Toggle is switchable. Issue #459 found it was silently ON (14.6x activation undercount). No test of toggling ON to measure activation VRAM savings vs compute-recompute cost tradeoff. High-impact if savings >2 GiB without excessive compute overhead.
verdicts.covering_evidence: Issue #459 corrected activation estimate but did not test toggling; no issue assigned to gradient checkpointing tradeoff exploration.

decisive_experiment.intervention: Add --gradient-checkpointing {on|off} flag; implement code branch to enable/disable at backbone_forward. Verify default OFF per contract.
decisive_experiment.measurement: Run two matched blocks (one ON, one OFF); log max VRAM during backward pass, total step time.
decisive_experiment.kill_condition: If activation VRAM reduction (ON vs OFF) is <1 GiB, claim savings are marginal; if step time ON is >20% slower than OFF, claim compute overhead is too high; either condition alone blocks adoption.

verdicts.target: BARRIER 1: MEMORY TRAFFIC / Lever: Optimizer-state quantization (fp32→int8/int4)
verdicts.reason: Proposal calculates 4× savings (16.6 GiB host RAM → 4.15 GiB) via int8 quantization on file-backed state. File-backed storage (issue #619) already in place. Quantized training never tested; CUDA correctness, convergence impact, and dequant overhead all unknown.
verdicts.covering_evidence: No issue assigned to optimizer-state quantization.

decisive_experiment.intervention: Implement int8 quantization layer: (a) at checkpoint save, float32→int8 via symmetric per-group scale+zero_point; (b) during step, stream int8→float32 dequant on-demand. Add --quantized-optimizer flag.
decisive_experiment.measurement: Log host storage size (before/after), disk I/O volume per step, step time, final loss after stabilization.
decisive_experiment.kill_condition: If storage doesn't shrink to <5 GiB (fail ≤4× compression), experiment fails; if step time increases >15% (dequant overhead), claim cost is too high; if final loss deviates >0.5% from baseline, claim quantization hurts convergence.

verdicts.target: BARRIER 1: MEMORY TRAFFIC / Lever: Front-load memmap allocation to low-commit phases
verdicts.reason: Issue #627 R4 explicitly implements this: move .grad.f32 creation from first step (78.93 GiB, crash point) to optimizer-init (65 GiB). Measured result: block-05 commit now 74.5 GiB (vs prior 78.9 GiB before front-load). Lever is implemented and measured.
verdicts.covering_evidence: Issue #627 R4; measured_position shows block-05 74.514/79.603 GiB (93.6% full) after front-load applied.

verdicts.target: BARRIER 1: MEMORY TRAFFIC / Lever: Intra-step allocation pattern (direct copy into persistent memmap)
verdicts.reason: Issue #627 external ruling proposes: eliminate per-param fresh FP32 grad allocation by direct-copying into pre-allocated memmap. CPU-only probe passes (bit-equal to baseline). CUDA semantics (async, stream ordering, overlapping writes) never validated. High-risk, high-reward (could eliminate transient peaks).
verdicts.covering_evidence: Issue #627 mentions proposal and CPU-only probe; CUDA validation never attempted.

decisive_experiment.intervention: Modify cpu_offload_adamw.py: replace fresh alloc + copy_ with direct memmap write. Pre-allocate gradient memmap at optimizer init; reuse same buffer each step. Create CPU-only variant first for validation.
decisive_experiment.measurement: CPU-only: verify bit-equality to baseline via buffer comparison. GPU: run single step, profile memory allocator (e.g., malloc_stats via glibc), measure peak transient VRAM.
decisive_experiment.kill_condition: If CPU-only memmap is NOT bit-equal to fresh-alloc baseline, implementation is incorrect; if GPU peak transient remains >4.5 GiB (unchanged), overhead masking prevents benefit; if step time increases >5%, overhead negates savings.

verdicts.target: BARRIER 1: MEMORY TRAFFIC / Lever: Layer freezing or sparse param updates
verdicts.reason: Issue #480 disclosed deviation: 45 of 185 params had zero state at checkpoint (layers 15-19 reset fresh). Proof-of-concept that sparse state is handled. No systematic freezing strategy implemented. Potential savings ~2 GiB optimizer state (45 params × 8B/param).
verdicts.covering_evidence: Issue #480 mentions zero-state at checkpoint; no systematic freezing strategy or planned work.

decisive_experiment.intervention: Identify 5 early layers (0-4) with low gradient variance (similar updates across timesteps, low per-param divergence). Implement --freeze-layers {0-4} flag; skip optimizer updates for frozen params.
decisive_experiment.measurement: Log optimizer state size (with/without freeze), step time, loss trajectory (50 steps, unfrozen baseline vs frozen config).
decisive_experiment.kill_condition: If optimizer state reduction is <500 MiB (negligible vs 16.6 GiB total), claim savings are marginal; if step time doesn't improve, claim optimizer isn't the bottleneck; if loss diverges >1% after 50 steps, claim freezing hurts convergence.

verdicts.target: BARRIER 2: OPTIMIZER-STATE COST / Gap: Live state dict size per optimizer-class logging
verdicts.reason: Conservative estimate 8B/param documented; audit calculates actual weighted 5.08B/param (140 Muon @4B + 44 AdamW @8B). Neither per-Muon nor per-AdamW class sizes logged per-run. Cannot validate stability across different model shapes or drift over time.
verdicts.covering_evidence: No issue assigns per-run state-size logging by optimizer class.

decisive_experiment.intervention: Add logging at checkpoint save: for each optimizer param, emit JSON row with {param_name, optimizer_class, state_dict[param].nbytes}. Aggregate per-class after load.
decisive_experiment.measurement: Extract per-class mean bytes from logs; verify Muon ≈4B, AdamW ≈8B; compute weighted average across all params.
decisive_experiment.kill_condition: If Muon averaged <3.8 B/param or AdamW averaged >8.5 B/param (outside expected range ±5%), claim conservative estimate is stale and needs re-calibration.

verdicts.target: BARRIER 2: OPTIMIZER-STATE COST / Gap: Muon momentum pre-seeding optimization (lines 206-209)
verdicts.reason: cpu_offload_adamw.py lines 206-209 pre-seed Muon momentum buffer. Whether fresh allocation or reuse path is faster remains unverified micro-optimization, low impact but measurable.
verdicts.covering_evidence: No issue tracks optimizer initialization micro-tuning.

decisive_experiment.intervention: Implement two paths: (a) current fresh allocation, (b) pre-allocated reuse from prior checkpoint. Add --muon-momentum-reuse {fresh|reuse} flag. Measure latency for 10 consecutive optimizer inits.
decisive_experiment.measurement: Log time per init path; compute mean and std of initialization latency.
decisive_experiment.kill_condition: If reuse is <20% faster than fresh, claim benefit is marginal; if no measurable difference, claim optimization is not applicable.

verdicts.target: BARRIER 2: OPTIMIZER-STATE COST / Gap: Post-checkpoint-load commit profile (blocks 2-10)
verdicts.reason: Front-load (issue #627 R4) reduces block-1 cold-launch commit. Blocks 2-10 resumes carry different profile (weights/grads already loaded). Never separately traced. Cannot confirm front-load suffices for all blocks or if blocks 2+ have hidden peaks.
verdicts.covering_evidence: Issue #627 addresses block-1 init; no issue traces block resumptions.

decisive_experiment.intervention: Add governor checkpoint immediately after block resume (right after checkpoint load, before first step of block N). Log commit level at each block resume.
decisive_experiment.measurement: Collect commit at block-1, block-2, ..., block-10 resume (single run across full 10-block sequence). Compute delta and identify peak block.
decisive_experiment.kill_condition: If any block-2+ resume commit is ≥74 GiB (matching block-05 observed), claim front-load doesn't cover resumptions; else claim all resumes are safe.

verdicts.target: BARRIER 2: OPTIMIZER-STATE COST / Gap: Memmap filesystem-paged access patterns (I/O locality, page faults)
verdicts.reason: File-backed optimizer state (184 .momentum.f32 files) accessed during each step. Sequential vs random access patterns, page-fault rate, and I/O latency are unmeasured. Could impact step-time variance or commit expansion cost.
verdicts.covering_evidence: No issue tracks I/O access patterns or page-fault profiling.

decisive_experiment.intervention: Run test block under Windows ETW with kernel VirtualMemory (page-fault) and FileIO (disk read/write) providers enabled.
decisive_experiment.measurement: Extract page-fault rate (major/minor faults per step), I/O latency histogram (read-wait time in ms), I/O pattern (sequential vs random via file offsets).
decisive_experiment.kill_condition: If page-fault rate is <10 per step and I/O latency is <10ms per read, claim I/O is not a bottleneck; if either exceeds threshold, investigate further.

verdicts.target: BARRIER 2: OPTIMIZER-STATE COST / Gap: Quantized-state training (int8/int4)
verdicts.reason: File-backed optimizer state (issue #619) enables int8/int4 quantization. Quantized training never tested; CUDA correctness, convergence impact, and dequant overhead unknown. Same lever as BARRIER 1 Lever 3.
verdicts.covering_evidence: No issue assigned to quantization.

decisive_experiment.intervention: Implement int8 quantization layer: (a) at checkpoint save, float32→int8 via symmetric per-group scale+zero_point; (b) during step, stream int8→float32 dequant on-demand. Add --quantized-optimizer flag.
decisive_experiment.measurement: Log host storage size (before/after), disk I/O volume per step, step time, final loss after stabilization.
decisive_experiment.kill_condition: If storage doesn't shrink to <5 GiB (fail ≤4× compression), experiment fails; if step time increases >15% (dequant overhead), claim cost is too high; if final loss deviates >0.5% from baseline, claim quantization hurts convergence.

verdicts.target: BARRIER 2: OPTIMIZER-STATE COST / Lever: Momentum buffer consolidation (184 files → single giant file)
verdicts.reason: Proposal: consolidate 184 separate .momentum.f32 memmap files into single giant file with per-param index. Improves filesystem metadata overhead and I/O locality. Unimplemented; impact on step time unknown.
verdicts.covering_evidence: No issue assigns consolidation.

decisive_experiment.intervention: Implement consolidated file format: single .momenta.f32 (giant buffer) + index JSON ({param_name: {offset, length}}). Rewrite CPU-offload to index into consolidated file.
decisive_experiment.measurement: Log filesystem metadata cost (file handles, inode lookups via ETW), step time, I/O IOPS distribution (consolidation vs per-file).
decisive_experiment.kill_condition: If step time worsens or stays flat (consolidation overhead not amortized), claim refactor not worth doing; if metadata overhead remains >5% of step time, claim benefit is marginal.

verdicts.target: BARRIER 2: OPTIMIZER-STATE COST / Lever: State dict resume pre-touch (anticipatory paging)
verdicts.reason: Streamed load (issue #627 point 3) active. Checkpoint load is high-commit peak. Proposal: pre-touch memmap pages at __init__ to avoid page-fault cascades at first step. Unimplemented; could smooth expansion latency.
verdicts.covering_evidence: Issue #627 mentions streamed load; no pre-touch strategy mentioned.

decisive_experiment.intervention: Add pre-touch phase at optimizer init: iterate memmap pages sequentially, touch each (read first byte) to fault into RAM. Measure pre-touch latency and post-init commit level.
decisive_experiment.measurement: Log time for pre-touch phase, commit at optimizer init (with vs without pre-touch), first-step page-fault count.
decisive_experiment.kill_condition: If pre-touch latency exceeds 5 seconds (unacceptable at init), claim cost is too high; if commit doesn't reduce or first-step faults don't decrease, claim benefit is negligible.

verdicts.target: BARRIER 2: OPTIMIZER-STATE COST / Lever: Momentum history transplant across rung boundary
verdicts.reason: Issue #513/#587 implements momentum transplant across rung boundary: layers 0-14 FF transplant, layers 15-19 reset fresh. Issue #480 discloses result: 45 params zero state at checkpoint. Lever is active and measured.
verdicts.covering_evidence: Issue #513/#587; issue #480 shows outcome (45 zero-state params, layers 15-19 reset).

verdicts.target: BARRIER 2: OPTIMIZER-STATE COST / Lever: Optimizer routing per-layer (Muon FF vs AdamW embed/norm)
verdicts.reason: Design-time fixed choice (Muon routes to FF layers, AdamW to embed/norm). Routing is hardcoded at model build, not adjustable at runtime. Changing requires model architecture re-spec and retraining from scratch. Not a local runtime lever.
verdicts.covering_evidence: Audit states 'FIXED design; no runtime adjustment' — architectural constraint, not operational lever.
